reason: The existing mapping of Articles 5, 9, and 15 provides a defensible and sufficiently complete regulatory basis. Article 5 prohibits harmful AI practices, including manipulative techniques and exploitative systems. Article 9 mandates a risk management system to identify and mitigate risks, including those from harmful outputs. Article 15 requires cybersecurity measures to protect against attacks that could alter outputs or performance, directly addressing the control of malicious code and harmful content. Together, these provisions support the control objective of managing sensitive data, malicious code, harmful content, and prohibited-use outputs.

challenge_comment: The control objective requires a multi-faceted approach. Article 5 addresses the prohibition of harmful outputs, Article 9 ensures a systematic process to manage associated risks, and Article 15 provides the technical cybersecurity foundation to protect the system and its outputs from manipulation. This combination effectively covers the control statement.
